answers.description: A Python pipeline that reconstructs textured 3D models from photogrammetry image sets by orchestrating OpenMVG (SfM) and OpenMVS (MVS).
answers.problem: Running OpenMVG/OpenMVS by hand is a long, error-prone chain of binaries and flags; there is no reproducible, resumable, recorded way to go from captures to a textured mesh.
answers.users: EduceLab internal researchers first (PGS scans and other capture sets, via Docker/Apptainer on workstations and the cluster), with the external cultural-heritage imaging community as secondary users.
goals: Reproducible & resumable: every run is recorded in a manifest and can be resumed or re-planned without silently inheriting stale state.
Easy deployment: published Docker/Apptainer images run identically on workstations and the cluster.
answers.voice: Concise and direct: short, need-to-know statements; minimal prose.
answers.languages: Python (currently >=3.9, EOL; minimum to be raised) + C++17/C++20 utilities via CMake 3.17+ superbuild. No frontend, backend framework, or database.
answers.python_min: 3.12 (target; setup.cfg still says >=3.9). Implies Ubuntu 24.04 base image and dropping 22.04.
answers.infrastructure: As-is (Docker on ghcr.io amd64+arm64, CPU + CUDA 12.4/12.8 on Ubuntu 22.04, built by GitHub Actions; Apptainer + SLURM; GitLab CI tests) plus planned migration to Ubuntu 24.04 for Python 3.12.
answers.commits: Descriptive imperative subjects, no prefix format; one branch + GitLab MR per track.
answers.review: Required for non-trivial changes (human or /code-review); trivial fixes may merge after self-review.
answers.checkpoints: Manual verification only at track completion.
answers.existing_conventions: Fresh from templates; recommend adopting ruff and clang-format as a future track.
